Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory) (EPM I) of the Jurisdiction and Agency Compliance and Enforcement Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) will oversee a unit within Section One. The unit is responsible for compliance and enforcement related to the Integrated Waste Management Act (AB 939), State Agency and Waste Management Act (AB 75), Mandatory Commercial Recycling law (AB 341), Mandatory Commercial Organics Recycling law (AB 1826), Short-lived Climate Pollutants law (SB 1383), and solid waste laws and regulations in the Public Resources Code (PRC) and California Code of Regulations (CCR). The incumbent will provide first line supervision for Environmental Scientist (ES) staff, applying principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, knowledge of statistical methods or analysis, integrated waste management and industry economics, public health, resource management, assessment, review and analysis of technical documents, review and analysis of operations and monitoring records, inspection of businesses, public agencies, solid waste facilities, and public spaces, and enforcement of AB 939, AB 75, AB 341, AB 1826, and SB 1383. The incumbent will oversee staff’s determination on the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety and the environment for the programs; provide oversight, training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards while also providing technical expertise, training and assistance to staff on evaluation and enforcement matters; review findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensure that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to waste diversion laws. The incumbent accomplishes this by: preparing and reviewing environmental documents to determine the effects of proposed activities on the environment; developing regulations and enforcing environmental and state minimum standards; developing recommendations regarding environmental programs; preparing and editing scientific data to develop environmental policies; reviewing business/facility environmental practices; and consulting with and advising other agencies and institutions engaged in related regulation and investigations.

For more information, please see attached the duty statement.

About The Company

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.

In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.

Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.

Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.

Our Company Values Guide Our Daily Actions

Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.

STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.

Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.

Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.

The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.

Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

Job Summary

The Data Analyst serves as a vital partner in guiding student affairs and enrollment-focused departments toward data-informed decision-making. This role is a key liaison between Student Affairs, Institutional Effectiveness (IE), Information Technology (ITS), the Division of Enrollment and Student Affairs, and the Division of Academic Affairs. The data analyst is responsible for developing and improving processes through data analysis and visualization. The data analyst collects and analyzes institutional data from various sources to identify trends in student performance, retention, and graduation. Reporting directly to the Associate Vice President for Access, Success, and Belonging, the data analyst is responsible for creating and maintaining a variety of deliverables, including dashboards and reports, for both SEM units and senior leadership. A core responsibility is promoting data literacy by training stakeholders and communicating actionable insights and recommendations at key leadership meetings. The analyst collaborates closely with ITS and IE to ensure data accuracy, compliance with governance standards, and overall process efficiency.

Responsibilities

The duties include, but are not limited to:

DATA COLLECTION AND MANAGEMENT: Gather and support the governance of data from various sources, such as student engagement platforms, student information systems, and surveys, to track student performance and success metrics. Collaborate with IE to ensure analytics tools are compliant with institutional data governance, regarding user access within business intelligence environments. Partner with respective Data Steward(s) and Data Governance Coordinator in IE to validate and document data deliverables (e.g., dashboards) within the Data Cookbook, ensuring data accuracy and compliance with AU's data governance framework. Collaborate with IE to ensure that analytics tools follow institutional data design standards and are included and up-to-date on AU's Analytics Roadmap. Collaborate with IT to improve data integrity and availability within business intelligence solutions sourced from data warehousing.

DATA ANALYSIS: Apply statistical and analytical techniques to identify trends, patterns, and key factors related to student success, retention, and graduation rates. Analyze data against research questions/hypotheses and use critical-thinking skills to develop the most appropriate methodologies and solutions. Conduct exploratory analyses on data to find actionable insights using appropriate methodologies.

REPORTING AND VISUALIZATION: Create reports, dashboards, and visualizations to present data findings in a clear and concise manner, enabling stakeholders to make data-driven decisions. Develop dashboards, queries, and data analyses for the SEM unit to improve their business processes and operations. Analyze unit-specific, institutional, and external data to develop deliverables for senior leadership, allowing them to track SEM performance. Updates data deliverables on a regular schedule. Responds to assigned ad-hoc requests via the Institutional Data Request process.

DATA INTERPRETATION AND ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS: Translate data into actionable insights that inform student affairs programs, interventions, and policies. Analyze, interpret, and summarize data that deliver actionable insights and empower decision-makers to achieve goals outlined in the SEM Plan.

COLLABORATION AND COMMUNICATION: Work with faculty, staff, and administrators to understand their data needs and communicate findings effectively. Promote data literacy by training SEM units and their immediate stakeholders, such as Directors, to interpret data deliverables and provide guidance on new and updated dashboards, analyses, and queries to ensure they can effectively use the information. Promote data literacy by communicating actionable recommendations and key insights from senior leadership data deliverables at cyclical leadership meetings such as the President's Cabinet, Lead Team, and the Directors' Meetings. Communicate data availability and updates from respective SEM units to the AU Data Community to promote awareness and support the SEM Plan goals. Summarize and communicate results effectively in a variety of formats, including executive summaries, reports, dashboards, and data visualizations.

PROCESS IMPROVEMENT: Identify areas for improvement in data collection, analysis, and reporting processes to enhance efficiency and accuracy. Collaborate with the respective unit's SIS Functional Analyst to promote data accuracy, user access, and coordinate data collection needed for data deliverables (e.g., dashboards, analyses, reports, slide decks). The Data Analyst is not expected to work directly in the data system (e.g., Banner, Slate) as the SIS Functional Analyst.

MAINTAIN AWARENESS OF DATA PRACTICES AND TRENDS: Stay informed of emerging technologies, methodologies, and best practices in higher education analytics, ensuring Augusta University remains at the forefront of data-driven student success strategies.

You’ll sit embedded with those teams to understand their work deeply and turn their hardest questions into answers, dashboards and analyses that drive decisions.

We're excited to hire this role at Range's Headquarters in McLean, VA. All of our positions follow an in-office schedule Monday through Friday, allowing you to collaborate directly with your team. Be the analytical partners that business units rely on. Embed with the teams you support, learn their work deeply and become the person they come to when they need to understand what’s happening or decide what to do next.

Own the dashboards your business units run on. Build and maintain the dashboards the business units rely on for day-to-day decisions. Set the conventions for what's authoritative vs. exploratory within those teams, in line with the company-wide standards.
Handle ad hoc support and questions with judgment. Be the first point of contact when business teams need a quick answer, a pull, or a check on a number. Know which questions deserve a five-minute answer and which deserve a real investigation.

5+ years of experience in a data-focused role (Data Analyst, Analytics, Data Science, or similar), including time embedded with business teams.
Advanced SQL. You can write a complex query without thinking about it and use it to answer the question that was asked, not just the question that was easy to query.
Comfort working in a modern data stack (dbt, a cloud warehouse, a BI tool like Sigma, Looker, or Tableau).

You're comfortable with Python for analyses that go beyond SQL — statistical work, hypothesis testing, anything that requires more than aggregations.

Chronicle Heritage is seeking Archaeological Field Technicians to support project work out of our Dexter, Michigan office. 4 months or more of experience conducting survey fieldwork

Experience performing pedestrian surveys, excavating/recording shovel test units, and recording archaeological sites
Knowledge of Michigan material culture - Indigenous and Euro-American history and prehistory
Experience with car camping and backpacking
Demonstrate excellent attention to detail, a positive work ethic, reliability, and commitment to working both independently and in a team environment
Previous experience with mapping equipment and other special application equipment (GPS, tablets, etc.)

Position Description

The Project Coordinator contributes to the overall success of CR Meyer and its heavy industrial customers through supporting the project team during the planning, budgeting, construction and post-construction project phases. Works collaboratively as a team to ensure the project meets CR Meyer’s safety guidelines, as well as all designated quality, schedule and budget requirements.

Works collaboratively with the Project Manager and the rest of the project team in estimating and executing construction projects.
Using a general knowledge of construction principles and design specifications, assists in preparing bids for customers.
Participates in the active implementation of the CR Meyer Risk Control Plan for all projects, and shares in the responsibility for maintaining a safe job site working with the customer, on-site staff, Safety Coordinator and the whole project team.
Assists in preparing budgets and schedules for construction project execution.
Prepares POs for all project-related expenses, tracks labor hours, processes expense sheets and prepares invoicing.
Tracks and maintains subcontracts and vendor information.
Coordinates the movement of assigned equipment, tools, supplies and other resources needed to complete the job and controls losses.
Assists in the tracking of productivity factors and documents them for future reference.
Keeps the Project Manager informed of any situations that require attention, maintains open lines of communication with the project team and may act as a back-up to the Project Manager.
Participates in routine site visits for plan implementation, reviewing budget status, determining progress, communicating with the on-site team and ensuring safety/compliance standards.
Participates in periodic updates and regularly communicates with the customer, project team, field staff, subcontractors and all other interested parties to ensure construction projects stay within specifications, schedule and budget through completion.
Assists in making sure that the proper QA/QC standards and “means and methods engineering” procedures required for the project are implemented and within CR Meyer guidelines.
Learns and uses CR Meyer provided software to prepare all required documents and project management updates.
At project completion, participates in project close-out meetings as needed.
Properly documents completed projects to use as a reference in the future.
Wears all assigned PPE and observes CR Meyer safety guidelines at all times.
Due to project deadlines and demands, regular and reliable attendance is required.
Completes all related reports and paperwork in a timely manner.
Represents the CR Meyer brand in a positive, professional manner at all times.
All other duties as assigned.

Position Requirements

Previous experience in construction required, preferably with an emphasis in large-scale civil/structural projects.
